correctness.rationale: The transition-parity classification exhausts four transitions over 1–4 palindromic factors. For b!=d and c<min(a,e), the four-part case has c-1 free internal central-zero splits and exactly three cut-at-transition cases; the complementary cases have at most two optimal cut sets. The rational generating series follows by positive composition enumeration; integrating a uniform Dirichlet simplex gives the normalized density 4(1-3t)^3 and mean 1/45. Independent DP compared 7776 complete quintuples, 400 larger tuples and exact composition counts through length 30. Boundaries c=a,c=e,c=a+e,b=d,a=e and n=5..7 are explicitly handled. Finite checks are not infinite proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The new conclusion is a simultaneous exact solution for all five positive run lengths and an optimal-solution multiplicity distribution. Earlier palindromic-defect formulas involve counting distinct palindrome factors, not factorization cut sets. There is no demonstrated logical implication from the inspected prior theorems to the new full claim.

evidence: Minimum number of palindrome factors, palindromic k-factorization, palindrome pair decomposition, and count of optimal cut sets were distinguished by quantified outputs.
The closest full-text pair-factor source addresses the existence/quantity of two-palindrome factors, not the number of all globally optimal partitions for arbitrary five-run words.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The new invariant K is not palindromic length PL, a palindrome-pair factor count, or a count of distinct palindromic substrings. The classification includes all optimal positional cut sets and can grow linearly with a middle run length even while PL is uniformly at most four.

evidence: The principal inspected papers have definitions and structural/algorithmic assertions but no displayed full five-positive-parameter table or bivariate optimal-multiplicity series.
The standalone finite checks compare the proposed symbolic formulas to all compositions of lengths 5 through 30; these are independently generated checks, not previously published tables.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: No exact previously published table was found covering the full quintuple classification or the coefficient series. A negative search is not a uniqueness proof, and a hidden table remains a residual risk.

originality.rationale: Full-text comparison to Rukavicka 2020, Rubinchik–Shur 2020, Borchert–Rampersad 2015 and Rukavicka 2021 shows those works treat palindromic length, algorithms, palindrome-pair factors, and rich words, respectively. None inspected states or logically entails the full five-run positional-optimum multiplicity classification plus its marked generating function and limiting density. Pair-factor PL=2 characterization and generic algorithms are explicitly prior; unindexed equivalence remains a recorded risk.
residual_risks: Possible previously published specialized count of minimum palindrome partitions in a run-length family that was not indexed by searched terms.
Palindrome-pair literature may imply portions of the PL=2 cases, which are background and not independently claimed as novel.
A prior finite-run palindromic-defect computation gives a different factor-count invariant and does not establish uniqueness of this optimum-partition-count result.

value.rationale: The intrinsic combinatorial invariant counts ambiguity of optimum palindrome decompositions. The all-parameter five-run classification and sharp threshold that multiplicity first becomes unbounded at five runs are structurally motivated, and the marked rational series and nondegenerate Dirichlet/Beta limit resolve natural enumeration and probability questions. The results are not isolated small-size table extensions or generic algorithm restatements.
